**DJ942** is a medical diagnosis code designating haemothorax (bleeding into the pleural cavity). Within the Danish healthcare system, it serves as a critical data point for tracking adverse events in cardiovascular patients. Specifically, DJ942 is utilized in the clinical quality indicator that measures the incidence of severe bleeding among patients treated for [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1].

The code is part of a comprehensive methodology employed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to monitor the safety and quality of atrial fibrillation care. To ensure that all significant bleeding events are captured, the registry's severe bleeding indicator relies on a broad spectrum of ICD-10 diagnostic codes. Alongside DJ942 and other respiratory or urinary bleeding codes like [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]], the framework includes codes for intracranial bleeding (such as [[di60|DI60]], [[di61|DI61]], [[di62|DI62]], [[ds064|DS064]], [[ds065|DS065]], and [[ds066|DS066]]) and gastrointestinal bleeding (including [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] through [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]) [^src1]. 

The definition and application of DJ942 as a quality metric are consistently documented across consecutive annual reports from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database, including the 2023 and 2024 publications [^src1] [^src2]. This consistent tracking allows for standardized data collection and cross-regional comparisons of patient safety outcomes in Denmark.
